subtopic: TTFT and TPOT diagnosis / Metric decomposition
learningObjective: Diagnose per-metric bottlenecks (TTFT vs TPOT) from serving-side data.
stem: A team observes the following per-request metrics under moderate load. Select all diagnoses that are consistent with the data. (Choose all that apply.)
profileData:
Workload: 4K-token prompts on average, 200-token outputs. TP=1, batch scheduler = continuous batching.
  P50 TTFT: 800 ms
  P99 TTFT: 3.2 s
  P50 TPOT: 45 ms/token
  P99 TPOT: 60 ms/token
  GPU compute utilization during prefill windows: 92%
  GPU compute utilization during pure decode windows: 25%
  KV cache usage: ~85% of budget under steady load
  Preemption rate: 12% of requests are preempted at least once

options.text: P99 TTFT >> P50 TTFT combined with a 12% preemption rate is consistent with head-of-line blocking or queueing under load: new prefills wait for KV space, and preempted sequences pay extra prefill on resume. TTFT tail is largely a queueing / preemption problem.

P50 TPOT ~ 45 ms/token combined with decode-window utilization ~25% is consistent with decode being memory-bandwidth bound (low compute utilization, low SM occupancy per token, but bandwidth spent on weight and KV reads). Adding more compute density would not directly reduce TPOT.
Prefill compute utilization ~92% indicates prefill is memory-bound; the fix is to increase batch size for prefill to reduce arithmetic intensity, since bandwidth is the current bottleneck.

High KV cache usage (~85%) plus a nontrivial preemption rate is a symptom that batch size is constrained by KV memory; MQA/GQA if applicable, KV quantization, or shorter contexts are direct levers to raise effective batch and reduce preemption.

explanation: A is correct: preemptions extend affected requests' TTFT dramatically, showing up as P99 tails. B is correct: decode is bandwidth-bound so low compute utilization is expected; TPOT is set by memory bandwidth, not SM occupancy. D is correct: high KV usage pushes preemption; the direct memory-side levers are MQA/GQA, KV quant, and shorter context. C is wrong: 92% compute utilization means prefill is compute-bound; increasing batch would improve arithmetic intensity if we were memory-bound, but we're already compute-saturated.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: HoL/queueing + preemption explains P99 TTFT tail.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: low decode utilization with bandwidth-bound TPOT is the standard signature.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: high KV usage → preemption → memory levers apply.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: reverses the direction — 92% utilization already indicates compute-saturated prefill.

assumptions: Compute utilization is measured as active-SM fraction inside kernels.
Baseline model is a dense transformer (non-MoE).
nonImplications: Does not imply KV quantization is always safe accuracy-wise.
Does not imply preemption is always fixable within a single GPU; sometimes throughput-preserving preemption is intrinsic.

distractorRationales.C: Confuses utilization direction — 92% = compute-bound, not memory-bound.

performanceClaim.scope: TTFT tail and TPOT bottleneck diagnosis
